body:
Ross, 
It's all in the careful interpretation of what you read. Examine this
carefully.

> 
> TK expressly addresses the question of how to
> harness the energy of true-believing Nazis in
> his manifesto.  In paragraph 222, he writes:
> 
> "Presumably a true-believing Nazi, for instance,
> is very different from a true-believing leftist.
> Because of their capacity for single-minded devotion
> to a cause, True Believers are a useful, perhaps a
> necessary, ingredient of any revolutionary movement.

He uses the term "true believing" for both Nazis & leftists and says
that possibly True Believers can be useful to a revolution.


> This presents a problem with which we must admit
> we don't know how to deal.  We aren't sure how to
> harness the energies of the True Believer to a revolution
> against technology.

He just said he doesn't know how to deal with True Believers. 

  At present all we can say is that
> no True Believer will make a safe recruit to the revolution
> unless his commitment is exclusively to the destruction
> of technology.  If he is committed also to another ideal,
> he may want to  use technology as a tool for pursuing
> that other ideal
> (see paragraphs 220, 221).

Interpret this carefully. It does not say that Ted wants to recruit
Nazis for his revolution. It says that you have to be careful in
recruiting True Believers because their loyalties may lie with some
other cause besides Luddite/Anarchism.


> 
> In paragraph 227, he writes:  "yet not all activist
>  movements are leftist, and some activist movements
> (e.g., radical environmentalism) seem to include both
> personalities of the leftist type and personalities
> of thoroughly un-leftist types who ought to know better
> than to collaborate with leftists."

Here he says nothing about recruiting Nazis or subscribing to their
cause. All he says is that some activists are OK while others are
"leftist".

> You can get your information from the filtering of
> the press (and reports with key portions redacted),
> or you can read the plain language of the manifesto.

Which is what I just did. I didn't see ONE paragraph which implied that
Ted subscribes to the Nazi ideology.

Yes. And the way I interpret this passage is that Ted believes that
these "true believing Nazi types" MAY be useful to the

headers.Subject: Re: Kaczynski views on true-believing Nazis (from his writing)
